History rows and the assessment summary

Source: vignettes/history-tables.Rmd
history-tables.Rmd

Each MFRI stock repo keeps three history tables in data/, which the advice sheets and tech reports read:

  • data/assessment.csv: the assessment summary, one row per year and assessment year (the columns of hafroreports::hr_assessment_template());
  • data/advice_hist.csv: the advice for each fishing year;
  • data/tac_hist.csv: the TAC, entered by hand after it is set.

For a category 3 stock, dlsrules makes this assessment’s rows: assessment_summary() for the summary and advice_hist_rows() for the advice. rfb_ref_points_table() gives the reference point table. The category 3 stocks that use them are listed in vignette("rfb-rule") and vignette("chr-rule"); 25-wit is the simplest example.

library(dlsrules)

Simulated inputs 

set.seed(1)
years <- 1985:2025
b <- round(2000 * exp(cumsum(c(0, rnorm(length(years) - 1, 0, 0.15)))))
survey_index <- rbind(
  data.frame(index = "smb_harv", year = years, b = b,
             b_cv = round(runif(length(years), 0.12, 0.3), 2),
             n = round(b / 0.6), n_cv = 0.2),
  data.frame(index = "smb_rec", year = years, b = round(b / 5), b_cv = 0.3,
             n = round(rlnorm(length(years), log(1500), 0.4)),
             n_cv = round(runif(length(years), 0.2, 0.4), 2))
)

z <- 0.12 + 0.05 * sin(seq_along(1990:2024) / 4)
ldist <- expand.grid(length = 20:70, year = 1990:2024)
ldist$n <- round(
  2000 * plogis((ldist$length - 32) / 1.5) *
    exp(-z[ldist$year - 1989] * (ldist$length - 32) / 1.2 * (ldist$length > 32))
)
ldist <- ldist[, c("year", "length", "n")]

assessment_year <- 2025
ref_points <- ref_points_iloss(
  list(K = 0.147, Linf = 62.1, Lc = 33, F_msy_proxy = 1),
  index_series(survey_index, "smb_harv", year_end = assessment_year),
  method = "min"
)
prognosis <- rfb_advice(
  index_series(survey_index, "smb_harv"), ldist, ref_points,
  prev_tac = 1659, assessment_year = assessment_year
)

Assessment summary

For a category 3 stock the summary shows the biomass index as SSB, a recruitment index (abundance), and a fishing pressure measure as F or HR, each with 95% intervals where it has a CV.

For an rfb stock F is the fishing pressure proxy LF=M / Lmean (FMSY proxy = 1). fproxy_series() gives it by year; the years are arguments, because they change the table:

fp <- fproxy_series(
  ldist,
  Lc = ref_points$Lc,
  Linf = ref_points$Linf,
  year_start = -Inf,
  year_end = assessment_year - 1
)
tail(fp, 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>    year mean_length     f F_proxy
#>   <int>       <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1  2022        40.8  1.01   0.987
#> 2  2023        41.1  1.02   0.981
#> 3  2024        41.4  1.03   0.973

rows <- assessment_summary(
  survey_index,
  ssb_index = "smb_harv",
  rec_index = "smb_rec",
  fishing_pressure = fp,
  species = 25,
  assessment_year = assessment_year,
  ssb_ci = "lognormal",
  rec_ci = "lognormal"
)
tail(rows, 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 10
#>    year median_SSB low_SSB high_SSB median_recruitment low_recruitment
#>   <int>      <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>              <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1  2023       2627   1775.    3888.               2235           1194.
#> 2  2024       3098   1935.    4959.               2051            974.
#> 3  2025       3474   1930.    6255.               1099            700.
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: high_recruitment <dbl>, median_F <dbl>, species <dbl>,
#> #   assessment_year <dbl>

The last year has no F: the catch sampling of the assessment year is not complete. For a chr stock (04-whg), pass landings instead of (or as well as) fishing_pressure: landings / SSB index is shown as median_HR up to landings_year_end (default the year before the assessment year).

landings <- data.frame(year = 1985:2024, landings = round(b[1:40] * 0.25))
tail(assessment_summary(
  survey_index, ssb_index = "smb_harv", rec_index = NULL,
  landings = landings, species = 4, assessment_year = assessment_year,
  ssb_ci = "normal"
), 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>    year median_SSB low_SSB high_SSB median_HR species assessment_year
#>   <int>      <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1  2023       2627   1597.    3657.     0.250       4            2025
#> 2  2024       3098   1641.    4555.     0.250       4            2025
#> 3  2025       3474   1431.    5517.    NA           4            2025

The intervals are log-normal, x exp(∓1.96 CV), unless "normal" is asked for, x (1 ∓ 1.96 CV), which can go below zero for a CV above 0.51. 04-whg keeps the normal interval for its SSB index, as its old code; the other stocks use log-normal.

Advice history rows 

advice_hist_rows(prognosis, assessment_year)
#>   assessment_year advice_period advice advice_basis.en advice_basis.is
#> 1            2025     2025/2026   1975 Domestic advice Innlend ráðgjöf
advice_hist_rows(prognosis, assessment_year, n_years = 2)
#>   assessment_year advice_period advice advice_basis.en advice_basis.is
#> 1            2025     2025/2026   1975 Domestic advice Innlend ráðgjöf
#> 2            2026     2026/2027   1975 Domestic advice Innlend ráðgjöf

The advice is rounded to whole tonnes. With n_years = 2 (biennial advice, see vignette("stock-choices")) the same advice is entered for two fishing years. basis_en and basis_is set the basis column (04-whg: “CHR rule” / “CHR reglan”).

Reference point table 

rfb_ref_points_table(ref_points)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   I_lim I_trigger F_msy_proxy    Lc  Linf     K   trl
#>   <dbl>     <dbl>       <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1  1651      2311           1    33  62.1 0.147  40.3

Iloss (I_lim) and Itrigger are rounded to whole units of the index (tonnes). trl is LF=M.

Keep the published rows

The history files hold what was published, and a rerun must not change it. A run on later data gives a slightly different advice for an assessment year that is already published (a rerun of the cod assessment gave 201,355 t instead of the published 201,674 t). Each stock repo therefore has R/hist.R with update_hist(hist, new, template = NULL), built on hafroreports::hr_update_hist(). It adds the run’s rows only for assessment years that are not in the file yet. Placeholder rows, with every value NA (e.g. 2026,5a,NA in tac_hist.csv before the TAC is set), are not published, and the run’s rows replace them.

The rule on plain data frames, without hafroreports:

keep_published <- function(hist, new) {
  values <- setdiff(names(hist)[vapply(hist, is.numeric, logical(1))],
                    "assessment_year")
  placeholder <- rowSums(!is.na(hist[values])) == 0
  hist <- hist[!(placeholder & hist$assessment_year %in% new$assessment_year), ]
  new <- new[!new$assessment_year %in% hist$assessment_year, ]
  out <- rbind(hist, new)
  out <- out[order(out$assessment_year), ]
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

published <- data.frame(
  assessment_year = 2023:2024,
  advice_period = c("2023/2024", "2024/2025"),
  advice = c(1500, 1659),
  advice_basis.en = "Domestic advice",
  advice_basis.is = "Innlend ráðgjöf"
)
# A rerun of 2024 on today's data would give another number; the file keeps
# the published 1659 t and only 2025 is added
rerun <- rbind(
  transform(advice_hist_rows(prognosis, 2024), advice = 1702),
  advice_hist_rows(prognosis, 2025)
)
keep_published(published, rerun)
#>   assessment_year advice_period advice advice_basis.en advice_basis.is
#> 1            2023     2023/2024   1500 Domestic advice Innlend ráðgjöf
#> 2            2024     2024/2025   1659 Domestic advice Innlend ráðgjöf
#> 3            2025     2025/2026   1975 Domestic advice Innlend ráðgjöf

In the targets pipeline:

tar_target(
  advice_hist,
  update_hist(
    historical_advice_file,
    dlsrules::advice_hist_rows(rfb_prognosis, assessment_year,
                               n_years = advice_n_years)
  )
),
tar_target(
  assessment_hist,
  update_hist(
    template = hr_assessment_template(),
    historical_assessment_file,
    assessment_rows
  )
)

Pitfalls

  • The files are read, not written. The targets add this assessment’s rows in memory. After the advice is published, add the published rows to data/*.csv by hand, and check that the latest assessment’s row is there.
  • Header-only CSV files (e.g. tac_hist.csv of a stock without a TAC) read as character columns. Give readr::read_csv() the column types.
  • Template by name: pass template = hr_assessment_template() by name; update_hist()’s first argument is the history.
  • The F proxy years (fproxy_series(year_start, year_end)) and the index of the SSB column change the history table and are fixed in the stock’s config.R (vignette("stock-choices")).
